document_check.note: Li X, Xia J, Li Y, et al. Risk scores of incident mild cognitive impairment in a Beijing community-based older cohort. Front Aging Neurosci 2022;14:976126. It uses BABRI data: 1,174 of 5,921 participants (19.8%) had MCI at baseline by consensus Petersen criteria (p4), and 72 (7.8%) of 921 cognitively normal people with follow-up developed MCI (p5). This matches the cited context, with the qualifications in notes.

cited_result: Principal: baseline MCI prevalence of 19.8% (1,174 of 5,921) by consensus Petersen criteria in the BABRI Beijing community cohort (p4), cited in three of the four sentences. Secondary: 7.8% incident MCI among 921 people cognitively normal at baseline (p5).
tool_reason: The cited results are a prevalence estimate and an incidence proportion, not the paper's risk-score discrimination (AUC), which the review does not cite.

domains.domain: 1. Sample frame appropriate to the target population
domains.rationale: The frame was Chinese-speaking community residents aged 50 to 80, excluding anyone with neurological, psychiatric or systemic illness or psychoactive medication use. This is narrower than a general older population, and the recruitment frame is described only by reference (p2).

signalling.question: Was the sample frame appropriate to address the target population?
signalling.quote: Exclusion criteria included severe visual or hearing loss, neurological, psychiatric, or systemic illness, and psychoactive medication use.

domains.rationale: Recruitment is described as continuous enrolment of as many participants as possible, with details deferred to a previous paper. Random or census sampling is not described.

signalling.question: Were study participants sampled in an appropriate way?
signalling.quote: Enrolled study participants were followed-up every 2 or 3 years, and as many new participants as possible were continuously recruited.

domains.rationale: 5,921 participants is ample for a prevalence estimate.

signalling.question: Was the sample size adequate?
signalling.quote: In this sample, 1,174 subjects (19.8%) were diagnosed with MCI.

domains.rationale: Table 1 reports demographics, lifestyle and medical history by group, and the setting (Beijing community, 2008 to 2018) is stated (p2).

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: TABLE 1 Characteristics of the study sample at baseline.

domains.rationale: 5,921 of more than 9,000 enrolled were analysed, restricted to people with complete information (p2). People who refused the personal questionnaire were excluded. The number excluded for missing data, as opposed to dementia, is not given, and excluded people are not compared with those analysed.

signalling.question: Was the data analysis conducted with sufficient coverage of the identified sample?
signalling.quote: In this research, we used data from 5,921 subjects (NCs and those with MCI) with the complete information needed for the design of this study.

domains.domain: 6. Valid methods for identifying the condition
domains.rationale: Diagnosis was by consensus of two experts using Petersen criteria with a 1.5 SD normative cut-off and ADL/IADL criteria (p3). As operationalised, criterion 6 requires no impairment in non-memory domains, so the definition captures single-domain amnestic MCI.

signalling.question: Were valid methods used for the identification of the condition?
signalling.quote: Consensus diagnoses were assigned by two multidisciplinary experts.

domains.domain: 7. Condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all participants
domains.rationale: All participants received the same five-domain battery from trained testers, with MMSE exclusion at 23 or below (pp2-3). Inter-rater agreement for the consensus diagnosis is not reported.

signalling.question: Was the condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all participants?
signalling.quote: A group of students well trained by professional neuropsychologists performed neuropsychological testing and collection of personal information questionnaires.

domains.rationale: The numerator and denominator are reported, but the prevalence is a crude proportion with no confidence interval and no age or sex standardisation, in a sample aged 50 to 80 that is not population-based. I searched Results and Discussion for a confidence interval or standardised prevalence and found none.

signalling.question: Was there appropriate statistical analysis?
signalling.quote: The sex-speciﬁc prevalence was also determined (χ2 = 21.83, p < 0.001), with an MCI prevalence of 22.8% in men and 17.9% in women (Table 1).

domains.rationale: No response or participation rate is reported, and there is no comparison with non-responders.

signalling.question: Was the response rate adequate, and if not, was the low response rate managed appropriately?
signalling.quote: Searched for the number invited, participation or response rate and characteristics of non-responders; the document says only 'the recruitment strategies have been described in our previous studies (Yang et al., 2021)'.

overall: Some concerns (JBI prevalence checklist; measurement items 6 and 7 'Yes'; items 1, 2, 5, 8 and 9 'Unclear')
overall_rationale: MCI was identified by a standard consensus method applied uniformly to a large sample, so measurement is not the concern. The 19.8% comes from a continuously recruited volunteer cohort aged 50 to 80 with illness-based exclusions and complete-case restriction from more than 9,000 enrolled. No response rate, confidence interval or standardisation is reported. This leaves unclear risk that it misestimates community prevalence.

applicability.rationale: The criteria identify single-domain amnestic MCI in a sample aged 50 to 80 that excluded neurological, psychiatric and systemic illness, which is narrower than an all-subtype prevalence in older community residents.
